External Impact: Significant financial loss; Legal challenges (Customers, Regulators); Breach of Contract or SLA penalties in contracts are triggered.
Internal Response: Urgent triage, with a response up to disabling apps, sites, features. In theory, can pull in every technical resource to fix. Communicate with every affected user, on site, on social channels.
Comment: P0 is a "drop tools, start running" type situation. It could be an existential threat to the company. It could increase the burn rate by an order of magnitude. It could lose users permanently.
Example situations: * Sensitive data exposed in code or API calls * Crash on launch * New code causes giant spike in costs * Site breach * DB breach * Email or SMS exploitation * Financial data breach * User PII breach, invoking CCPA notification rules

Frequency: Significant number of people, more than 20%
External Impact: Users can't do something important in a major use-case. There is no workaround.
Internal Response: Immediate evaluation, with same-day fix being the ideal. Consider comms with users.
Comment: Most things work in the apps, except for X feature or when Y is true
Example situations: * Users cannot join events scheduled for today because of a timezone error. * Android users get crashes but only if they have Samsung phones. * Mobile app was (or will be) rejected for publication due to policy/legal violations.

External Impact: Users are blocked, inconvenienced, or confused. There are workarounds.
Internal Response: Eval and fix in the next release.
Comment: It's obviously broken and it's common.
Example situations: * Users are allowed to click post for bulletin board announcement, but cannot ultimately submit because they don't have permission to post announcements. The backend check was correct, and the fix is in the UI to stop confusing the users.

External Impact: Some users will not notice the problem. Others will prefer it work differently. It annoys a few people.
Internal Response: Eval and fix sometime, perhaps never. Could wait until folded into related fixes or designs.
Comment: It's sort of broken and it's generally uncommon.

External Impact: Most users will not notice or care.
Internal Response: Generally won't be fixed unless there's a legal or contractual requirement related to the issue.
Comment: Good bugs to give an incoming intern, so they learn the build, test, release processes.

External Impact: No user will understand the impact directly.
Internal Response: They sit in the backlog for a long time, perhaps to be cleaned up with a rewrite of related functionality. Or they get re-evaluated later when their causes are understood better, e.g., the initial numbers were low because it was caused by testing of a new OS update, or there was a bug in this common library that was finally fixed.
Comment: Some people believe these bugs shouldn't be filed.   I'm in favor of filing them because of unknown causes. Better to file it now as a known issue, and maybe update or re-prioritize later with more details. A bug isn't a contract that has to be filled or fixed.
